findings.evidence: `nl -ba .../ContractableLaw.lean` shows raw forall hypotheses at lines 54-56, 93-95, and 101-103, while `PathSpace/Law.lean:52` has `ExchangeableLaw.map_permReindex ... (hρ : ExchangeableLaw ρ)`.
findings.fix: Change those hypotheses to `hρ : ContractableLaw ρ`, matching `measurePreserving_reindex` and `ExchangeableLaw.map_permReindex`; keep only `contractableLaw_iff` as the explicit unfolding lemma.
findings.issue: `ContractableLaw.map_reindex`, `ContractableLaw.map_shift`, and `ContractableLaw.map_shift_iterate` take the unfolded defining forall instead of `(hρ : ContractableLaw ρ)`, exposing the body as part of the public eliminator API.

findings.evidence: `rg` confirms only whole-path/shift API in this file (`ContractableLaw.map_reindex` at line 54 and measure-preserving iff at line 69); the analogous exchangeable path API exists as `ExchangeableLaw.map_prefixProj_of_injective` in `PathSpace/Law.lean:85`, and the needed strict extension lemma is `exists_strictMono_nat_extending_fin` in `PermutationExtension.lean:30`.
findings.fix: Add a characteristic lemma such as `ContractableLaw.map_prefixProj_of_strictMono` and, ideally, an iff against all strict finite selections, using `exists_strictMono_nat_extending_fin` and `map_reindex_prefixProj`.
findings.issue: The predicate has no public finite-marginal characterization, so a user cannot derive the contractability statement `ρ.map (fun x => fun i : Fin n => x (k i)) = ρ.map (prefixProj α n)` for strict finite selections without unfolding and reproving the extension argument.

summary: The new path-law predicate is useful, but its public API still exposes the defining forall in core theorem signatures and does not provide the finite-dimensional marginal characterization users need to consume contractability without unfolding.
